kv.memory.bd-create-parallel-race: Do not parallelize 'bd create --silent &' calls against the same database. The SQLite ID assignment races; two children of the same epic can collide on the same .N suffix, causing one creation to silently drop. Mitigation: chain sequential 'bd create ... && bd create ...' instead of parallel '&'. Verified during 2026-05-12 session — lost a bead in a 4-way parallel batch under epic fig9; had to recreate sequentially.
kv.memory.blocked-sender-suppression-any: Blocked-sender suppression: any new ephemeral event delivery feature in JMAP Chat (typing, presence, reactions-in-flight, read-receipts-in-flight, etc.) must include a blocked-sender check in the normative draft, not just in the guide. Pattern: if sender is on recipient's blocked list (ChatContact.blocked=true), the event MUST be silently dropped. Main draft :1473 establishes this for messages; extension to ephemeral signals prevents a blocked user from leaking presence/attention pattern. Found missing for ChatTypingEvent in WSS draft (filed as dim0); ChatPresenceEvent had it. Audit any new ephemeral type the same way.
kv.memory.fig9-broadcast-mention-storage: fig9 broadcast-mention storage: per-user mentions stay in Message.mentions; broadcast-scope mentions in Message.broadcastMentions (new array; defaults to []); rich-body uses 'mention' span (userId) and new 'broadcast' span (scope). When bodyType is application/jmap-chat-rich, BOTH Message.mentions AND Message.broadcastMentions MUST be empty. Push computation for mentionScopes (fig9.4) must UNION over Message.broadcastMentions[].scope AND rich-body 'broadcast' spans .scope — same dual-path pattern as f86f4f4's hasMention fix for user mentions in ex4u. The 'mention_all' permission was renamed to 'mention_broadcast' in the main draft as part of fig9.2.
kv.memory.jmap-chat-spec-kq1-r2-assessme: jmap-chat-spec-kq1 R2 assessment: 15% confidence of missed bug. Real complaints exhausted. Channel exemption (line 439) resolves P0 jmap-chat-spec-0fw.26 as design choice. Missing {#chat-typing} anchor is only residual editorial issue. No round 3 needed.
kv.memory.jmap-cid-design-decisions-1-sh: jmap-cid design decisions: (1) SHA-256 only, lowercase hex, field named sha256. No multihash/IPFS CID. Complements JMAP-BLOBEXT digest:sha-256 (base64, Blob/get) without conflict. (2) Standalone capability urn:ietf:params:jmap:cid. Sections structured to also serve as upstream patches to RFC 8620 upload response and JMAP-FILENODE FileNode object.
kv.memory.mention-information-is-stored-: Mention information is stored in TWO places in JMAP Chat depending on bodyType: (1) Message.mentions array (Mention[]) for text/plain and text/markdown; (2) inline spans of type 'mention' with userId field for application/jmap-chat-rich (Message.mentions MUST be empty in that case per main draft :1257). Any cross-document rule that 'checks Message.mentions' is silently wrong for rich-body. Affects push hasMention (filed as ex4u), and likely other places to audit: notification/badge logic, mention queries, federation Peer/deliver mention extraction. fig9.4 (broadcast-mention scope) adds a third storage dimension.
kv.memory.push-draft-mentionscopes-is-pe: Push draft mentionScopes is PER-RECIPIENT, not per-message. Server computes the candidate set from Message.broadcastMentions[].scope UNION rich-body 'broadcast' spans .scope, then filters to scopes for which the receiving account owner is in the locally-resolved recipient set. This is what makes mentionUrgency elevation correct for @here and @admins where only some recipients qualify under the deployment's predicate. A non-targeted recipient of an @here message gets mentionScopes:[] and does NOT get mentionUrgency elevation. Field added in fig9.4 commit replacing the old hasMentionAll boolean.
kv.memory.typing-notifications-nearly-ev: Typing notifications: nearly everything about them should use SHOULD/MAY not MUST/SHALL. They are best-effort ephemeral signals, not reliable protocol obligations.
